# `world/PlanetPhysics.js`

> **Source:** `engine/world/PlanetPhysics.js`

PlanetPhysics.js - Rotating Planet with Dynamic Gravity Simulates a spherical planet with: - Rotation (angular velocity, quaternion orientation) - Radial gravity field (direction + magnitude based on position) - Surface-relative coordinate transforms - Double-precision position (via hi/lo f32 split) Key Features: - Shell theorem: Gravity only from mass "below" you - Variable gravity by depth (surface → core) - Coriolis effect for moving objects - Day/night cycle from rotation Coordinate Systems: - World: Absolute coordinates (f64 via hi/lo) - Planet-Local: Relative to planet center - Surface-Local: Relative to a surface point (tangent space)

### `splitDouble(value)`

### `combineDouble(hi, lo)`

Combine hi/lo f32 pair back to double

## Constants

- `G` — Gravitational constant (scaled for game)
- `DEFAULT_PLANET_RADIUS` — Default planet radius (180,000 km = 180,000,000 m)
- `DEFAULT_PLANET_MASS` — Default planet mass (for Earth-like surface gravity)
- `DEFAULT_ROTATION_PERIOD` — Default rotation period in seconds (24 hours)
- `MIN_GRAVITY` — Minimum gravity magnitude (to avoid division issues)

## Notes & Examples

### World Streaming & Scenes

The world system manages scene graphs, asset streaming, and level transitions. Scenes are entity hierarchies with spatial indexing (BVH) for fast culling and raycasts. Worlds stream assets asynchronously with priority based on distance and visibility.

**Example: Scene graph and streaming**
```js
import { World } from 'engine/world/World.js';
import { Scene } from 'engine/scenes/Scene.js';
import { Entity } from 'engine/ecs/Entity.js';

const world = new World();
const scene = new Scene();
world.addScene(scene);

// Create hierarchy
const player = new Entity('Player');
const camera = new Entity('Camera');
const weapon = new Entity('Weapon');

player.addChild(camera);
camera.addChild(weapon);  // Weapon follows camera

scene.add(player);

// Stream in a level
await world.streamLevel('level1', {
  priority: 'high',
  bounds: player.boundingBox,
  onProgress: (pct) => console.log(`Loading: ${pct}%`)
});

// Spatial query: find entities in radius
const nearby = scene.querySphere(player.position, 50);
```
